title: Jesus our groom part 3
scripture_text: “Do not let your hearts be troubled. You believe in God believe also in me. My Father’s house has many rooms; if that were not so, would I have told you that I am going there to prepare a place for you? And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come back and take you to be with me that you also may be where I am. You know the way to the place where I am going.” Thomas said to him, “Lord, we don’t know where you are going, so how can we know the way?” Jesus answered, ‘I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me. If you really know me, you will know my Father as well. From now on, you do know him and have seen him. Philip said, “Lord, show us the Father and that will be enough for us.” Jesus answered: “Don’t you know me, Philip, even after I have been among you such a long time? Anyone who has seen me has seen the Father. How can you say, ‘Show us the Father’? Don’t you believe that I am in the Father, and that the Father is in me? The words I say to you I do not speak on my own authority. Rather, it is the Father, living in me, who is doing his work. Believe me when I say that I am in the Father and the Father is in me; or at least believe on the evidence of the works themselves. Very truly I tell you, whoever believes in me will do the works I have been doing, and they will do even greater things than these, because I am going to the Father. And I will do whatever you ask in my name, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son. You may ask me for anything in my name, and I will do it.’’
devotional:
When Jesus says to Thomas that he is ‘the way’ he is saying that intimacy and devotion are essential for faithfulness in this troubling world. Like us, Thomas did not get what Jesus was saying. Thomas was thinking in terms of directions, he wanted a road map, a how to. But he needed to change his thinking, he needed to recalibrate his understanding. I do not think Jesus was thinking about or referring to heaven when he said these things. But he was trying to teach his disciples how to remain faithful in times of trouble.

During the period between the ERUSIN and the NISUIN the bride had to remain completely faithful and exclusive to the groom. They could not ‘disengage,’ The only way of breaking the covenant made at the ERUSIN was through divorce. So she needed to wait, not knowing when her groom would return for her.

To know Jesus as ‘the way’ is to view him in the same way a young Middle Eastern bride would see her groom. For her, all her hopes, dreams, desires, expectations and longings are in her groom. He is the way to her future. He is more than an acquaintance, he is not some kind of add-on to her life, he is her life, He is her future.

Let us take a step back and ask ourselves some hard questions.

Do we really want Jesus to be ‘the way’?

Do we have the emotional ability to so invest our lives in Jesus that we know that all my future hopes and dreams depend on an intimate relationship with him?

Some of us may need to rediscover the way. We feel lost and disconnected, we live more like jilted lovers than expectant brides. We have lost the joy of our first love, we have no intense desire or consuming passion for the one we used to love. We need to rediscover the way, for if we don’t our lives will be reduced a dry religious statement instead of a dynamic relationship.
prayer: Father thank you that placing all our hope in Jesus is ‘the way’.
